title: Negligence — duty, breach, causation, and damage

content.overview: Negligence in Indian tort law requires a duty of care owed to the claimant, breach of that duty by falling below the standard of the reasonable person, and damage to the claimant caused by that breach, subject to remoteness and defences.
content.study: Structure every problem as duty → breach → causation (factual and legal) → damage. Duty is framed by foresight and proximity (Donoghue/neighbour principle as received in India). Breach compares conduct to the reasonable person in the circumstances. Causation uses but-for and intervening-cause analysis; remoteness limits recoverable loss. Pair with strict liability (no need to prove fault) and vicarious liability (when an employer answers for a servant).
